full_judgment: 11. It appears that both the parties adduced necessary documents to substantiate their respective case. The trial court though relying on the documents of the plaintiffs decreed the suit but the appellate court on meticulous examination of the documents produced by the contesting defendants found out that the admitted owner Maimuna Khatun settled the suit land in favour of Krishna Kanta Chakravorty by registered pasta dated 30.05.1927 and that the genuineness of this registered patta was proved from the relevant papers relating to Rent Suit No.1201 of 1931 and Rent Execution Case No.340 of 1932 the exhibited-D and J. The said documentary evidence proved it sufficiently that Maimuna Khatun filed that rent suit against Krishna Kanta Chakravorty for arrears of rent. The appellate court, therefore, rightly found that the registered patta dated 30.05.1927 showing settlement of the suit land in favour of Krishna Kanta Chakravorty by Maimuna Khatun was genuine one. This fact of settlement of the suit land to Krishna Kanta Chakravorty by Maimuna Khatun in the year 1927 makes out the plaintiffs case that one Md. lshaque purchased the suit land in auction in the year 1935 not true. It appears that the appellate court, on careful examination of the documents filed by the plaintiff, detected rightly that in the year 1935 the taluki right of Maimuna Khatun was sold in auction for arrears of rent and Md. Ishaque purchased the taluki right only of Maimuna Khatun in that auction. The appellate court also made Clear observation to the effect that at the time of purchase of taluki right by Md. Ishaque in the year 1935 Mallika Bala Dry and Tulshi Bala Dey were in possession of the suit land as tenants and that the plaintiff could not adduce any iota of evidence before the court to prove that the auction purchaser Md. Ishaque ejected those tenants from the suit land. The appellate court found out also that in the registered sale deed of the year 1956 executed by Mallika Bala Dey in favour of the defendant No.1 Mvi. Abdur Rashid (the purchaser from the auction purchaser Md. Ishaque) was men Boned as owner of the taluk. This fact also indicates sufficiently that Md. Ishaque purchased the taluki right only of Maimuna Khatun in auction held in the year 1935 and subsequently he sold that taluki right to Mvi. Abdul Rashid in the year 1943 and that Mallika gala Dey and Tulshi Bala Dey were the tenants under Md. Ishaque and thereafter under Mvi. Abdur Rashid. Admittedly, the P.S. khatian of the suit land has been recorded in the names of the defendant Nos.1 and 2 who acquired the suit land from Mallika Bala Day and Tulshi Bala Dey.
